headline: Some birds have told me that Iran expects Israel to enter the conflict in the coming hours or days, leading to the resumption of a full-scale war. The problem is that Iran appears ready to repeat the same mistake. To my knowledge, Iran possesses military satellites, which it uses to identify and maintain target banks across the region. I was also told that, in 2025, Iran leased access to a Chinese satellite. In addition to its own satellite capabilities, Iran is receiving intelligence support from both Russia and China. Even with the expectation that a new war could be imminent, I haven't heard of any serious plans for a large-scale preemptive strike against U.S. and Israeli assets in the region to inflict maximum damage and relieve some of the pressure. One thing I am confident about, based on what I've been told, is that Iran is currently capable of launching more than 200 ballistic missiles in its opening salvo. However, there are concerns that doing so would expose a large number of launchers, making them easier to detect and destroy. Instead, the thinking seems to be to stick with the same "shoot-and-scoot" strategy used during the last war. From Iran's perspective, it worked: they lost only a few launchers (two documented), which is a remarkably low number considering the intensity of the conflict.
